The recommended decision

Adopt one explicit transition contract per subsystem owner, with a shared vocabulary for outcomes and effects, and derive capabilities, diagnostics, workflow guidance and conformance checks from those owned contracts.

An incremental internal architecture decision. Preserve host-specific behavior and the existing native transaction kernel. No repository changes were made by this audit.

The recurrent failure is a disagreement between state owners: a producer creates a state its consumer rejects, a completion or readiness label combines distinct facts, or a retry repeats a side effect whose outcome was already committed. The recommendation is to make those boundaries explicit and testable.

Independent axisTypical observationsRequired distinction
Progresspending, active, review, completed, blocked, retiredA user or agent can update progress without manufacturing verification or authorization.
Evidenceabsent, current, stale, contradicted, partial, unavailableA result names the source revision, scope and producer; stale proof does not silently rewrite historical progress.
Authorityunestablished, granted for exact scope, denied, revoked or expiredA transition description is not an authority grant. Existing explicit user and host constraints remain controlling.
Deliverynot requested, intent recorded, attempted, observed, outcome unknownCommitted local state and successfully delivered external effect are different facts. Unknown outcomes require observation before retry.
Execution and containmentqueued, running, cancel requested, quiescent, cleanup failedA process exit, timeout request or closed UI is not proof all writers/resources stopped.
Identity and generationsubject revision, input digest, operation id, owner/session/epochCallbacks and retries must remain bound to the exact operation and owner. Cancellation/disposal invalidates stale UI updates and ordinary execution authority; explicitly owned cleanup and outcome reconciliation remain permitted until settled.

Contract contents

Each owner declares: owner and contract version, subject identity and generation, state before, event with typed payload, guards and actual authority binding, next state, effect intents and their owning executor, observed effect outcome, user-facing disposition and machine-readable reason, retry/recovery rule, compatibility invariant.

Keep existing stable IDs, schema/wire fields, operation-id replay, before-image history, canonical serialization and registered file ownership.
Keep ordinary progress assistive. A missing optional attestation must not become a new permission ceremony or universal blocker.
Preserve actual hard stops, explicit authority and host capability limits. Do not repair Pi child authors by bypassing unavailable confirmation or audit controls.
Retain product/host and explicitly approved timing exceptions. Manual Project sync-now and merge-observed issue effects are not interchangeable.
Use small ordinary Go/Python/TypeScript definitions and pure decisions where useful. A general statechart DSL, database, background daemon and single global machine are unnecessary.
Do not claim transactional rollback of a remote publication, message or merge. Reconcile actual outcome and use the owner’s documented recovery.

Acceptance criteria across all three experiences

ExperienceExpected improvementHow to verify it
UXTruthful visible status and next action; no additional ordinary-work prompts; user changes survive uninstall; canceled UI/resources stay canceled.Exercise success, refusal, interruption and resume from the user-facing owner. Record extra prompts and misleading readiness/empty-success states.
DXOne owner for each capability, output class, state vocabulary and retry rule; generated derivatives stay consistent.Change a contract once, regenerate the dependent catalog/schema/diagnostics, and prove all handlers/producers/consumers conform.
AXDiscoverable current state, valid events, evidence scope, effect result and exact recovery action.Require an agent to choose the next action from structured results without inferring permission, completion or retry safety from prose labels.

No finite audit can guarantee that every future change always improves all three experiences or never breaks anything. The enforceable objective is explicit compatibility invariants, measured acceptance criteria, discriminating event-sequence tests, exact-artifact checks and rollback for each migration slice.

Confirmed findings and material contradictions

The status on each finding states the evidence level. A bounded probe is not an installed-host or release test. The complete finding records are also preserved in the JSON ledger.

W-F01Workflow and resource contractssource-confirmed documentation or policy contradiction

Conflict command prescribes a broader stop than the assistive engine contract

Detail

The conflict command says all work stops when governing rules conflict. Current sprint/context guidance and ADR0043 describe refusal scoped to dependent work. These cannot both be a universal rule. Source does not implement a single dependency-aware conflict controller.

Recommendation

Choose and document the stop scope explicitly. Recommend stop affected authority/data dependencies, preserve independent read-only work, and keep genuine global host/user stops global. This is a policy decision, not a silent prose cleanup.

W-F02Workflow and resource contractssource-confirmed documentation or policy contradiction

Debug handoff treats a correctable packet error as a terminal one-shot boundary

Detail

The workflow forbids repairing and resubmitting any rejected packet. The validator is stateless and distinguishes malformed/invalid packets from internal I/O errors; it records no consumed one-shot capability. The prose therefore imposes an extra recovery policy beyond implementation.

Recommendation

Separate invalid input, denied authority, stale binding and internal failure. Permit an explicitly corrected new input attempt where authority remains valid; retain the refusal for an unchanged denied request. Requires approved workflow-policy change.

Maintenance severity and reviewer disposition conflict

Detail

The dependency reviewer can report HIGH maintenance risk while saying not to block on maintenance alone. The included reviewer contract says every HIGH is blocking and additions never replace that rule. This makes a correct verdict ambiguous for the reviewing agent and user.

Recommendation

Represent severity and disposition separately; document the explicit maintenance-only disposition exception or revise its severity. Generate the common verdict contract from the selected policy.

W-F04Workflow and resource contractssource-confirmed recovery gap

Terminal finding harvest has no implemented recovery for interruption before the terminal step

Detail

Several workflows harvest qualifying findings at completion. The knowledge helper and session/standup paths do not implement a durable pending-harvest backstop. An interrupted run can therefore leave eligible findings only in conversation; the source does not prove every such finding is lost.

Recommendation

Keep harvest opportunistic. If durable recovery is desired, record bounded pending candidates at discovery and settle/deduplicate on completion/resume. Register any new output with all native readers; do not introduce a new universal completion gate.

W-F07Workflow and resource contractssource-confirmed documentation or policy contradiction

Watch confuses absence of agent polling with absence of CLI polling

Detail

The watch command describes gh pr checks --watch as server-side blocking with no polling interval. The official gh command documents --interval with default10seconds. Waiting in one detached CLI invocation avoids model-driven polling, but the underlying CLI still refreshes periodically.

Recommendation

Say one detached gh watch process with no repeated agent calls; preserve its timeout/cancel behavior. Correct the no-polling claim.

Ordinary context previews poison strict snapshot output recognition

Detail

contextOrdinaryPreview calls PutDerived("context-previews"), but internalOutputsWith does not allow that reserved directory. Any successful preview therefore creates a directory that a subsequent strict Snapshot refuses as UNRECOGNIZED_OUTPUT. Completion normalized workspace scanning shares the same recognizer. Ordinary progress can still work; strict verification, review/quality/farm consumers can fail.

Recommendation

Add a closed validated context-preview output contract and exercise preview→snapshot→completion composition. Do not broadly ignore arbitrary .artifacts contents.

Retirement with retained task checks or scope baselines is rejected as orphan state

Detail

syncExecution removes retired live task states but retains task_check_observations and existing scopes. Changes appends tombstones under retired_symbols. symbol.Build gives these tombstones Kind=retired_symbols; planStructure accepts historical checks for nonlive IDs only when Retired and Kind=tasks, impossible for the emitted tombstone. render.Prepare calls Structural, so task retirement after task-check fails ORPHAN_STATE. ADRs are decisions, not execution evidence

These assessments compare current implementation with the relevant decision text. The recommendation preserves decisions that remain useful and calls out specific clauses that require correction or an intentional new decision.

Decision sourceAssessment
.codearbiter/decisions/0043-assistive-state-engine.mdline 1
Direction supports explicit state/evidence separation and ordinary progress without permission ceremony. It does not prohibit a compile-time transition registry. Existing strict optional paths must not become the default again. Task-block/STale and SMARTS resets need explicit semantic review against this principle.
.codearbiter/decisions/0037-extensible-structured-artifact-engine.mdline 1
Keep small kind-neutral file/CAS/journal kernel and closed per-kind contracts. Do not interpret accepted architecture as proof of implementation or a requirement for one mega state machine. It explicitly permits splitting proven boundaries if generic machinery harms correctness.
.codearbiter/decisions/0045-merge-observed-github-work-effects.mdline 1
Supports staged intent, explicit sync, uncertainty reconciliation, no remote rollback claim. Manual Project sync-now is an explicit approved exception to issue after_merge timing; do not mistakenly homogenize it. Mapped effects add their own frozen generation/timing guards.
.codearbiter/decisions/0012-dual-host-store-concurrency-parity.mdline 1
Historical campaign scope exception is not a permanent ban on locking/CAS; current native engine already has both. Do not cite it to reject common race hardening now.
.codearbiter/decisions/0004-database-free-stdlib-only-architecture.mdline 1
Database-free remains consistent. Literal "no schema layer", "file-based prose", and "no transactional guarantees beyond append-only files" are superseded by implemented typed schema, HTML and journaled multi-file transactions plus ADR-0037. Do not add a database merely to model states; update historical/active claim classification.
.codearbiter/decisions/0040-independent-per-target-release-with-consumer-safety-gates.md
Status: accepted in source; implementation compared rather than presumed Supported: Independent per-target jobs, immutable existing-tag check, exact asset readback and dormant Codex npm helpers are implemented. Conflicts: Its universal rerun recovery claim has C-F01 counterexample. Its release-skill pre-tag advisory policy conflicts with required CI in C-F03. Decision: Keep independent target publication and immutable artifact rules. Define a per-target completion predicate and govern the enforcement-class inconsistency; do not reintroduce cross-target cohort locking.
.codearbiter/decisions/0044-trusted-pi-npm-publication.md
Status: accepted in source; live npm account configuration not observed Supported: Active publish command uses OIDC provenance and no static token fallback; exact integrity, signatures and repo/workflow/source attestation gate finishing GitHub release, including recovery of existing versions. Limits: Source inspection cannot verify npm trusted-publisher account configuration or an actual successful release. ADR explicitly requires live qualification. Decision: Retain fail-closed identity gate and pending-draft recovery; expose pending registry/attestation states with their deadline and next action.
.codearbiter/decisions/0030-orchestration-mode-plane-with-composed-persona.md
Its per-session-and-mode cache description conflicts with its promise of injection on each mode change. The reproduced A→B→A sequence suppresses the return injection. Bind delivery to current selection/generation/content and amend the cache contract; do not treat the accepted text as proof that transitions work.
.codearbiter/decisions/0036-bounded-authorization-cleanup-direction.md
Retain bounded authorization and actual host/user hard stops. Explicit state contracts can carry existing authority without new approval ceremonies. Any removal of a current confirmation or change in authority semantics is a distinct reviewable decision.
.codearbiter/decisions/0040-independent-per-target-release-with-consumer-safety-gates.md
The ordinary CI candidate path makes a nominally advisory pre-tag command a gate, and published-without-receipt is not admitted by the outer recovery eligibility path. Reconcile those facts with the ADR rather than claiming its rerun/advisory intent is implemented.
.codearbiter/decisions/0044-trusted-pi-npm-publication.md
This decision changes Pi publication trust/provenance. It does not by itself supersede the unrelated pre-tag advisory rule or repair the published-release receipt recovery admission gap.

Sequence tests that distinguish real behavior

Mode A→B→A; mode marker write succeeds then audit append fails; dispose while sidebar metrics are pending; preview write→strict snapshot; accepted launch binding→completion consumer; check history→task retirement; local commit/merge→final report failure→recovery; Release published→receipt attachment fails→rerun; timeout/overflow→cleanup failure→retry; inventory unavailable→display; user edits spinner setting→uninstall.

For each sequence, assert observable effects and retained state, not only return codes or line coverage. During extraction, compare old and new behavior on existing inputs and fail on any unexplained difference. Intentional bug fixes are named exceptions, reviewed independently.

Evidence, coverage and exact boundaries

The audit inventories the entire pinned Git tree and reads the primary implementation/workflow owners. Full text, complete executable content, targeted reads, byte-verified shared copies and renderer-verified derivatives are distinguished per file. Historical reports, most tests, fixtures, static assets and external dependency internals are not misrepresented as independently audited current implementations.

Decisions and remaining verification

Decisions requiring user approval before remediation

DecisionConcrete scope
Conflict scopeWhether a document-level conflict pauses only dependent work, with global host/user stops still global.
Debug and reviewer policyWhether corrected malformed packets can be resubmitted, and how severity differs from gate disposition.
Progress versus evidenceWhether task-block/reconcile invalidation changes progress markers, evidence applicability, or both; define migration before changing old records.
Pi child authorsEither implement an actually supported scoped parent delegation/audit path, or advertise the child capability as read-only until that exists.
New durable interruption recoveryWhether to add a registered bounded residue record for terminal harvest; keep ordinary work nonblocking.
Governance changesAmend the specific ADR/compatibility/release-policy clauses that conflict with the selected implementation, using the normal acceptance owner.

These decisions do not block the completed read-only audit. They identify the intentional semantics changes that must be separated from compatible refactoring and defect repair.

Verification still required

  1. Native Go branches were fully read, but no Go toolchain was available in this workspace. Native composition failures are source-confirmed, not claimed as executed native integration tests.
  2. The Python and Node probes use actual repository functions with temporary fixtures or injected host/Docker/terminal adapters. They do not constitute installed Claude, Codex or Pi host qualification.
  3. No npm publication, GitHub Release mutation, remote Project/issue write, real Docker containment run or farm provider inference was performed. Publication and process recovery findings use source analysis and bounded pure probes.
  4. Verify native writer/reader closure, launch-binding limits and tombstone preservation on the supported OS/architecture matrix and exact distributed binaries.
  5. Exercise Pi activation/child tools/sidebar under the supported actual host runtime; verify cancellation and callback ordering with real UI and process lifetimes.
  6. Exercise farm process-tree containment and report recovery with injected timeout, cleanup failure and final report-write failure; prove no surviving writer can race a reset/retry.
  7. Exercise sandbox Docker output overflow, cancellation and failed removal; verify workload quiescence independently from client exit and preserve unknown inventory/cleanup outcomes.
  8. Exercise release publication failure after the Release becomes public and before final codearbiter-publication.json attachment; rerun must complete missing evidence without retagging or republishing.
  9. Qualify each exact released payload independently. Source on main, an accepted ADR, a successful packaging validator, or advisory exit0 is not a released-behavior guarantee.

Affected surfaces

Within this audit: core/artifacts; core/pysrc; core/surface; the generated ca, ca-codex and ca-pi payloads; Pi TypeScript extension; farm and sandbox tools; build/qualification scripts; GitHub CI/release workflows; and the in-repository documentation site. Other authorized organization repositories were not inspected or changed. Any later propagation into Academy or a separate product site requires its own exact-source compatibility check.

Recommended next action

Adopt the transition-contract decision, then implement the smallest first slice: native output writer/reader closure and operation discovery, with preview→snapshot and capability/dispatch consistency regressions. In parallel, keep the separately evidenced persona, Pi diagnostics/sidebar and release/farm recovery defects as separate reviewable fixes. Do not start with a whole-system rewrite.
